chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard my father asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and I was listening, so he said to him: 'Sometimes we instruct the man so he buys for us the land, and the house, and the slave, and the slave girl, and we make a fee to be for him'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.

key_terms.جُعْلًا: a fee or reward for a specific service
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a fee to a broker for purchasing property or slaves on one's behalf?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Sahl ibn Ziyad, confirms the permissibility of the brokerage fee (ju'l) for agents purchasing diverse assets including land, houses, and slaves, reflecting the practical economic needs of the Shia community. It underscores the validity of agency (wakalah) in commercial transactions, a principle widely accepted across Shia jurisprudence as evidenced by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I heard my father asking Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I was listening, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Sometimes we instruct the man so he buys for us the land, and the house, and the slave, and the slave girl, and we make a fee to be for him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“Once, a man asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when I was listening, ‘We perhaps order a man to buy for us land, house, slave or slave-girl and assign for him a certain amount. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
